simple.meaning: כֶּשֶׁף (kesheph) is a Hebrew word meaning “magic.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: כֶּשֶׁף (H3785) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 9:22, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Isaiah, Micah, Nahum.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כֶּשֶׁף (H3785) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in כֶּשֶׁף (H3785) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: כֶּשֶׁף (kesheph) / H3785 is traced through 2 Kings 9:22, Isaiah 47:9, Isaiah 47:12, Micah 5:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: When Joram saw Jehu, he said, “Is it peace, Jehu?”

I will cut off the cities of your land,
because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.

definitions.full: H3785. kesheph [ כֶּ֫שֶׁף ] noun masculine 2Kin 9:22 sorcery , only plural (Assyrian kišpu , id.); — כְּשָׁפִים Micah 5:11 ; Nahum 3:4 ; suffix כְּשָׁפַיִךְ Isa 47:9 , 12 ; כְּשָׁפֶיהָ Nahum 3:4 ; 2Kin 9:22 ; — sorceries: 1 literal כ ׳וְהִכְרַתִּי מִיָּדֶיךָ Micah 5:11 , said of Israel; כ ׳רֹב Isa 47:9 , 12 || חֲבָרַיִךְ , said of Babylon. 2 figurative of seductive and corrupting influences : of Jezebel 2Kin 9:22 || זְנוּנִים ; of Nineveh personified as harlot Nahum 3:4 (|| id. ), called כ ׳בַּעֲלַת 3:4 (following זְנוּנֵי זוֺנָהמֵרֹב ).
